items.title: Kevin Feige, Marvel Studios, and Hugh Jackman Pay Tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart After Actor's Death at 86
items.description: Kevin Feige, president of Marvel Studios and COO of Marvel, has given a heartfelt response to the death of acclaimed actor Sir Patrick Stewart.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Kevin Feige, president of Marvel Studios and COO of Marvel, has given a heartfelt response to the death of acclaimed actor Sir Patrick Stewart.

Stewart, best known for his roles as Jean Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in Marvel’s X-Men films, died on Wednesday, October 28 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia. His family broke the news in a public statement on October 29.

As shared by Variety, Kevin Feige gave a touching eulogy to the celebrated actor and knight following the news of his death.

“I’ll never forget the first time I saw Sir Patrick Stewart on the set of the first X-Men,” Feige said. “After years of knowing him as the inimitable Captain Picard, I was in awe — and he turned out to be everything I had seen on screen and more: brilliant, charming, warm, generous, with a quiet strength and gravitas.”

“Away from the cameras, he was even more remarkable, with a wonderfully sharp sense of humor. It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed.”

Marvel Studios also released a statement after in a post on its official Twitter/X account.

“All of us at Marvel Studios are deeply saddened by the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from X-Men to Logan to Avengers: Doomsday. He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.”

Hugh Jackman, who starred alongside Stewart as Wolverine, also shared a tribute to the actor on Instagram, along with two photos from their time working together.

"We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days," he wrote.

Avengers: Doomsday marks Stewart’s final film performance, where he will reprise his role as Charles Xavier. He was 86 years at the time of his death, leaving behind a storied legacy of unforgettable performances in film, television, video games, and stage plays.

Marvel fans have gathered online to grieve together, with many quoting a line from Stewart’s Charles Xavier: “Just because someone stumbles and loses their way, it doesn't mean they're lost forever.”

All of us at Marvel Studios are deeply saddened by the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from "X-Men" to "Logan" to "Avengers: Doomsday." He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.

— Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) October 29, 2026

In lieu of flowers, Stewart’s family urged friends and fans to donate to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.

Image Credits: Rich Fury/Getty Images

items.title: Archive of Our Own Could Be Down for Up to 4 Weeks After Going Dark for Emergency Maintenance
items.description: Popular fanfiction site Archive of Our Own went down for maintenance early this morning. Now, the website is claiming it may take up to a month to come back online.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Popular fanfiction site Archive of Our Own, commonly known as AO3, went down for maintenance early this morning. Now, the website is claiming it may take up to a month to come back online.

At 3:26am ET, AO3_Status acknowledged that the site was down for maintenance. Two hours later, the account claimed maintenance was expected "to take at least 12 hours." Then, at 1:59pm, a new post revealed that service restoration will take around two weeks, but it "could be up to" four, leaving dedicated readers without their favorite fanfic destination for the forseeable future.

The latest status update quickly went viral on X, picking up over 7 million views and 140,000 likes. Readers are shocked, to say the least, and have promptly exploded into an apocalyptic frenzy across social media.

We estimate that service restoration for #AO3 will take around 2 weeks but it could be up to 4 weeks. We are hopeful that we will be able to bring the site back up in a degraded state sooner. Refer to our status page for updates: https://t.co/YAyyoTDOpE

— AO3 Status (@AO3_Status) October 29, 2026


"WE ARE DOOMED" replied one user. "worst tweet in the history of this app. delete" said another.

Some dismayed fans are trying to report the issue up the political chain of command. “SOMEONE DO SOMETHING” says @uhbucky, tagging official government accounts like the CIA, FBI, and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and picking up over 20,000 likes.

While AO3 does undergo regular maintenance, the site rarely goes offline for more than 24 hours. However, the maintenance does appear to be becoming more regular. Just this past March, the service went down for three days following reports of a database server issue.

The Archive team has not revealed any information about the incident that prompted the maintenance period, or what exactly changed to extend it for such a long period. AI agents have been posing a new threat to online communities, and just last week, an exploited PHP vulnerability led to government demands for sites using PHP to implement extra security. It’s possible the PHP vulnerability has some connection to AO3’s current outage.

As for what readers can expect over the next couple of weeks, the AO3 status page explains that the team is 'hopeful' they’ll be able to launch a 'degraded' version of the archive while the full version undergoes maintenance. This would likely be a read-only version of the service, which hosted over 18 million works at the time it went down.

Users are still able to access any fanfic they’ve downloaded locally to their personal devices. Readers can also read their favorite fanfiction by inputting URLs into platforms like the Wayback Machine. However, as some users note, both of these options prevent authors from getting credit for impressions, Kudos, or comments during the maintenance period.

items.title: Sir Patrick Stewart Dead at 86
items.description: Acclaimed actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Acclaimed actor Sir Patrick Stewart (Star Trek: The Next Generation, the X-Men franchise) died today at the age of 86 following a brief battle with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

His family posted a statement about his death to social media on October 29, a day after his death on the 28.

“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” wrote family spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”

A veteran of the British stage blessed with a rich, commanding voice, Stewart was 47 when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation. The role vaulted the Shakespearean actor to international fame. Stewart would reprise the role for the TNG films, as well as his own spin-off streaming series Picard.

Stewart was cast as Professor Charles Xavier in 2000's X-Men in part because, as director Bryan Singer once jokingly said, Stewart was perfect as a bald man sitting in a chair giving orders. He played the character in the X-Men films and later in the MCU in both Doctor Strange and the Multiverse of Madness and in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, which will mark Stewart's final screen appearance.

Born on July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart's other film and TV credits include Excalibur, David Lynch's Dune, Robin Hood: Men in Tights, Green Room, Moby Dick, The Prince of Egypt, TMNT, The Sheep Detectives, American Dad, Ted, and I, Claudius.

For many years, Stewart played Ebenezer Scrooge in a one-man stage production of A Christmas Carol, reprising the role in a made-for-TV movie adaptation.

Stewart also voiced characters in video games such as Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, Forgotten Realms: Demon Stone, Lands of Lore: The Throne of Chaos and The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion.

In lieu of flowers, his family asks fans to send memorial contributions to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.

Image Credits: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images

items.title: PUBG is Getting a Live-Action Series on Netflix Written, Directed by, and Starring Donald Glover
items.description: Yep, you read that right: Grammy-award winning music artist and actor Donald Glover is directing and starring in a live-action series adapting Krafton’s battle royale game, PUBG.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Yep, you read that right: Grammy-award winning music artist and actor Donald Glover is directing and starring in a live-action series adapting Krafton’s battle royale game, PUBG.

PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds is getting the Hollywood treatment with a TV show that will be written, produced, directed by, and starring Donald Glover. His brother, Stephen Glover, is also involved in the project as a co-writer and executive producer.

Other executive producers on the series include Michael Schaefer for NEON TV, Fam Udeorji for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee for LV3H. As told in a press release shared with IGN, Krafton — the South Korean gaming conglomerate that owns the franchise — is intent on expanding the IP into “original entertainment content.” LV3H, its entertainment entity, is also helping develop and produce the series.

While making an entire series based on a game where 100 players are dropped onto an island to fight to the death might seem like a bit of a stretch, there’s actually some pretty deep lore that explains the ‘why’ of it all. Admittedly, PUBG was initially created as a purely multiplayer experience, but it has since been fleshed out with an encompassing narrative that can be read on its official website.

The long and short of it is that the Battlegrounds are the brainchild of a billionaire named Sergei Kalimnik, who was the lone survivor of a deadly Soviet attack on the fictional island of Erangel in 1965. After experiencing “17 days of conflict” and watching Soviet officials attempt to dispose of their victims’ corpses, he came up with the brilliant idea of eventually buying the island and recreating his childhood trauma on a grand scale — conscripting 100 people and forcing them to fight until only one remains.

It’s sort of like Squid Game, when you think about it; these experiments expanded to other locales, while audience of shadowy, untouchable elites, much like the VIPs from Netflix’s hit South Korean thriller series, watch from afar. According to the PUBG Universe page, this also somehow ties back to a centuries-old tradition called ‘Magna Venari: The Great Hunt’ that began in the early 15th Century. Described as the “hunting of human prey,” it sought to answer a single question: “Why do some survive when others do not?”

There’s, surprisingly, a lot for Glover to work with here. And given his talents in showbiz (Atlanta, Community, Swarm), I’m genuinely keen to see what he brings to the table from the PUBG world.

This is the latest video game to score a celebrity-led adaptation following news of Michael B. Jordan’s Battlefield movie. He, alongside Christopher McQuarrie, are reportedly shopping the adaptation around to different studios in hopes of bringing Electronic Arts’ popular military game series to the silver screen. Sony has emerged as a frontrunner to snag the film, though any other news remains nebulous for now.

Image Credits: Mila Gruber/WireImage via Getty Images

items.title: Celeste and TowerFall Developer Explains Why Games Were Abruptly Delisted from Xbox
items.description: Celeste and TowerFall have been delisted from Xbox, as the developer has chosen to boycott Microsoft for its involvement and investments with the Israeli government.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Celeste and TowerFall have been delisted from Xbox, as the developer has chosen to boycott Microsoft for its involvement and investments with the Israeli government.

Developer Maddy Thorson, the mind behind Celeste and TowerFall, confirmed on Bluesky that her team had removed the games from Xbox. They are no longer available to purchase on the platform, which caught some fans by surprise. Thorson stated that she made the decision to remove the titles in support of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement, which describes itself as a “Palestinian-led movement for freedom, justice and equality.” IGN has asked Microsoft for comment on the situation.

The movement targets companies that are involved with or invested in the Israeli government amidst the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine. Celeste and TowerFall are not the first games to drop Xbox as a result of this movement, either. Earlier this fall, the beloved co-op adventure game, Big Walk, chose not to release on Xbox and cited the boycott as its reason. The team noted that, should Microsoft divest from its Israeli ties and be removed from the list of BDS targets, Big Walk would be brought to Xbox.

"We have made the decision not to release Big Walk on Xbox, in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement’s call to boycott Microsoft, and their designation of Microsoft Games (and Xbox) as a priority boycott target," said Big Walk developer House House at the time. "If you need help understanding our motives, we would recommend reading about why Microsoft is a BDS priority target, the successes this kind of pressure has already had on Microsoft, and especially, watching this great introductory piece by People Make Games."

Celeste and TowerFall have both been out for some time, with the latter having been released in 2013 and the former in 2018. Both games remain available for purchase on PlayStation, PC, and Switch.

items.title: Assassin's Creed Valhalla Is Getting New Game+ 6 Years After Release
items.description: Assassin's Creed Valhalla launched all the way back in November 2020, but Ubisoft just announced that it's getting its own New Game+ mode.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Assassin's Creed Valhalla launched all the way back in November 2020, but Ubisoft just announced that it's getting its own new game+ mode.

In a blog post, Ubisoft laid out some of its future plans for Assassin's Creed. One of them is a tiny, yet cryptic, update on Assassin's Creed: Codename Hexe. It also announced new game+ mode for Valhalla a mere six years after it first hit consoles.

The new game mode will be coming on November 5, and will include a new, optional progression mode, along with new runes, achievements and a stash system. Ubisoft will also be adding a new crafting material, Mithril, which can be used to upgrade divine gear.

But on top of the NG+ mode, Ubisoft teased that Valhalla will be getting even more updates. In the post, Ubisoft says it will "share full details in the upcoming Patch Notes, along with news regarding current-generation console updates in the coming days." It's not clear what Ubisoft means by "current-generation console updates," but I'd bet on a nice little graphics boost.

While Valhalla does have a PS5 and Xbox Series version, the game hasn't received a PS5 Pro Enhanced glow-up, so I'd guess that's what Ubisoft meant by console updates. But even outside of the Pro, in the years since Valhalla came out, every console has been updated with better upscaling, whether that's QSSR on the base PS5 or FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series consoles.

Assassin's Creed was well received at launch. When IGN reviewed it, we gave it an 8, with reviewer Brandin Tyrrel saying, "Assassin's Creed Valhalla is a massive, beautiful open-world fueled by brutal living and the dirty work of conquerors. It's a lot buggier than it should be but also impressive on multiple levels."

The new game+ mode isn't the first time Ubisoft has slow-walked updates for Assassin's Creed Valhalla. Players also had to wait nearly two years to get Steam achievements, and the company was still fixing bugs with the game as late as January 2025.

items.title: Apex Legends Update Lets You Dual Wield the Wingman, Brings Back Lifeline Revive Shield
items.description: Some people are absolutely cracked with the Wingman. And now they’ll be able to use two at once. Cipher introduces Akimbo Wingman, which trades off some of the accuracy for big(ger) damage.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Apex Legends: Cipher is coming on November 3 and it’s bringing a new weapon style that makes me scared. The Wingman is a semi-automatic revolver that utilizes Sniper Ammo, and it’s been the bane of my existence since Apex Legends launched.

Some people are absolutely cracked with the Wingman. And now they’ll be able to use two at once. Cipher introduces Akimbo Wingman, which trades off some of the accuracy for big(ger) damage.

The Wingman has wavered a bit in recent seasons and sits as the 19th most effective weapon in DPS terms, but it’s still deadly in accurate hands, across basically any distance. It’s two-to-four headshots for a Wingman kill depending on the armor they’re wearing, which is what makes it so deadly in the right hands.

The Akimbo Wingman will push players in closer to barrel stuff your face. It’s going to be interesting to see where the weapon ends up with this new option — famously, the Akimbo Mozambique was famously nerfed quickly after it went from a barely used gun to the game’s dominant weapon.

On top of the dual revolvers, Crypto is getting a rework dubbed Crypto Rewired, which sees him role switch from a drone-camping git to a push-forward intel machine. items.title: Ubisoft Shares Cryptic Assassins Creed Codename Hexe Update
items.description: Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe was announced all the way back in 2022, but aside from a spooky teaser, we still don't know much about it. In a new blog post, Ubisoft has shared a cryptic clue that may shed some light on the project — if you're able to decode it, that is.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe was announced all the way back in 2022, but aside from a spooky teaser, we still don't know much about it. In a new blog post, Ubisoft has shared a cryptic clue that may shed some light on the project — if you're able to decode it, that is.

In the blog post, Ubisoft laid out its vision for the future of Assassin's Creed, and, of course, Codename Hexe is a big part of that future. At first glance, the update on the upcoming game is vague; the blog post simply says, "We're making steady progress on this darker Assassin's Creed experience, though there is still work ahead of us. We know the wait has been long, and we're grateful for your patience and continued enthusiasm for the project."

But it seems like more concrete updates will be coming next year, with the post continuing, "The team remains focused on delivering the unique vision at the heart of this project, and we'll share our next major update in 2027." That's pretty much all the information about Hexe that Ubisoft has shared, so it seems like we'll have to wait until next year to get some concrete information about the game.

Ubisoft did include a little clue for dedicated players with a knack for decyphering coded messages, though. After the Codename Hexe entry, Ubisoft simply writes: "ZKLWAVN MBEXNK ULYCNJ... LWY01... I#########F // QNTMAKHX TWTEMZL. YSIZKQ AADSWX NFAAMPHP.//" I'm not sure what that means, if anything, but I'm sure that fans will be able to decode it eventually.

Whatever it ends up being called, Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe is likely to be the first mainline Assassin's Creed game after 2025's Assassin's Creed Shadows. Other than the spooky theme of its only teaser, we don't know much about when it's going to take place, but I'd imagine that witchcraft is going to be a major theme.

We know little else about the game so far. Earlier this year, a leaker suggested a popular Assassin's Creed character would be returning. We've also heard that the game has been reworked internally to change some of its more magical elements. It has also gone through some staffing shakeups earlier this year, after the game director and creative director left the project.

items.title: Forza Motorsport Director and Turn 10 Boss Dan Greenawalt Retiring From Microsoft After 27 Years
items.description: Dan Greenawalt, a 27-year Microsoft employee who helped build Turn 10 Studios from scratch and directed eight Forza Motorsport games spanning all four Xbox console generations, is retiring from Microsoft, according to a new report.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Dan Greenawalt, a 27-year Microsoft employee who helped build Turn 10 Studios from scratch and directed eight Forza Motorsport games spanning all four Xbox console generations, is retiring from Microsoft, according to a new report.

The Verge's Tom Warren reports that he's seen an internal memo that confirms Greenawalt's departure. “Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft,” said Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams. Playground, who develops the Forza Horizon franchise, was merged with Greenawalt's Turn 10 last month as part of Xbox's ongoing "reset."

Williams added, in part, "It’s hard to overstate Dan’s impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original Xbox in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow."

Unfortunately, it looks as though 2023's Forza Motorsport, which was meant to be a platform of sorts that would be evolved and added onto, might be the last Motorsport game for the foreseeable future, if ever, after layoffs hit Turn 10 last year and reportedly relegated the remaining team to support duty on the highly profitable Forza Horizon. Motorsport will not be getting any more new content.

Greenawalt's Forza Motorsport series consistently earned critical acclaim, with all eight games scoring an 8 out of 10 or higher at IGN.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Reportedly Subtitled 'Sentinel,' New Story Details Revealed Ahead of Rumored Announcement
items.description: A new report claims that the next Elder Scrolls game will be titled The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, along with new story details.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
A new report claims the next Elder Scrolls game will be titled The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, along with new story details.

According to The Verge, The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is the title of the highly-anticipated follow-up to Bethesda's Skyrim. This title has been rumored for some time now, but The Verge is putting extra weight behind it. According to the outlet, the game's title could be formally announced as soon as next month, possibly aligned with either Skyrim's 15th anniversary or Xbox's 25th anniversary. The game will reportedly take place in Hammerfell and dive into the history of the titular artifacts, allowing players to discover their secrets firsthand for the first time.

All of this is pretty exciting and shows that the game is likely getting closer to release. While we're not quite sure when to expect The Elder Scrolls 6, it wouldn't be surprising if we hear more details next year ahead of a 2028 release. However, Bethesda does like to wait until its games are close to the finish line to really lay it all out there, so we may be waiting a while before we get raw gameplay.

The road to The Elder Scrolls 6 has been quite long, as Bethesda announced the game back in 2018. At that stage, the game was still in the very, very early stages of pre-production. It may not have even really been anything more than a concept at that point, since Bethesda was full steam ahead on Starfield, which wouldn't release for another five years from that point. Since shipping Starfield, The Elder Scrolls 6 has become a massive priority and the studio's focus going forward.

Although there is a lot happening in and around Bethesda with future Fallout games, re-releases, and Starfield updates, The Elder Scrolls 6 seems to be taking the bulk of the developer's focus. The only question now is: will it all be worth the long wait?

items.title: RAMageddon Will Only Get Worse in 2027, According to Samsung
items.description: The entirety of 2026 has been defined by an ongoing RAM crisis, causing price increases on everything from the PS5 to the Steam Machine. And, according to Samsung's latest earnings report, it's only going to get worse over the next year.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The entirety of 2026 has been defined by an ongoing RAM crisis, causing price increases on everything from the PS5 to the Steam Machine. And, according to Samsung's latest earnings report, it's only going to get worse over the next year.

In its Q3 2026 earnings call, it was shared that Samsung's semiconductor segment, which includes its memory business, made the company 147.1 trillion Korean Won, of which 106.5 trillion is profit. That makes up for 72% of all of Samsung's revenue in the last quarter. And according to Samsung, those numbers were possible by prioritizing the manufacturing of the HBM4 memory used in AI datacenters.

Looking forward, Samsung expects the memory market to tighten even more in 2027, with the company claiming "Surging AI-driven demand likely to further tighten supply shortages compared with CY26," when talking about the memory business next year. AI demand is so strong that Samsung doesn't even mention consumer-grade DDR5 memory, and is instead focused entirely on building a "stable sales base through long-term contracts and ensure timely readiness of new products tailored to requirements for AI applications."

This earnings report comes just a couple months after a Digitimes report suggested that all memory capacity for 2027 had already been sold through. And, according to Samsung's earnings, that Digitimes report seems like it was accurate, even if the company is working to expand manufacturing to make, well, more RAM for AI data centers.

Samsung is one of just three major memory manufacturers in the world right now, and all three have prioritized manufacturing hich capacity server-grade memory for AI datacenters rather than anything that you'd find in a gaming PC. As early as December last year, Micron killed off Crucial, its consumer-facing memory and storage brand.

There have already been signs that the RAM crisis is worsening, as well. A couple of weeks ago, the PS5 Pro sold out, causing the price of used consoles to skyrocket to $1,399. And, earlier today Xbox CEO Asha Sharma claimed that demand is outstripping supply for consoles, even if the Xbox Series X and Series S are still widely available right now.

items.title: Original GTA Artist Says He's 'Flattered' to See His Influence Continue in GTA 6 Cover Art
items.description: Stephen Bliss, the former Rockstar Games artist who helped establish Grand Theft Auto's iconic visual style, has said he's flattered to see elements of his original designs continue to appear in the cover art for GTA 6.
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Stephen Bliss, the former Rockstar Games artist who helped establish Grand Theft Auto's iconic visual style, has said he's flattered to see elements of his original designs continue to appear in the cover art for GTA 6.

Speaking to IGN at Lucca Comics and Games, Bliss, who worked at Rockstar from 2001 to 2016, reflected on his contribution to the series and how his work continues to influence its visual identity, even a decade after his departure.

"Well, I looked at the GTA 6 cover, for example. I had nothing to do with that, but the fact they still use the box grid and they still put the helicopter in the top left corner, which was something that I developed, I'm flattered by that," Bliss said. "It touches me that that heritage continues. And my influence is in the GTA 6 cover, but it's its own language. I just have little references in there. I'm like, 'Oh, that's nice that they used that.' But I'm absolutely not saying I contributed to that massively."

Bliss was instrumental in establishing the comic book-inspired look of Grand Theft Auto's promotional artwork, including the grid layout that has become synonymous with the franchise. However, he was also keen to emphasize the contributions of other Rockstar artists, including Anthony Macbain and Steven Olds.

Bliss explained that while he's spent the past decade establishing his own artistic identity outside Rockstar, he remains grateful for his time working on the series and the impact it continues to have.

The full interview with Bliss also explores how the September 11 attacks influenced the GTA 3 cover art, and the creative challenges behind the distinctive visual styles of Vice City and San Andreas. Check it out here.

items.title: Pokémon Happy Meals Are Coming Back to McDonald's — Here's What Cards and Toys Are Included This Year
items.description: Pokémon Happy Meals are coming back to McDonald's, and the fast-food giant has officially confirmed what toys and cards you can collect from this round of the promotion.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Pokémon Happy Meals are coming back to McDonald's, and after a series of leaks hit social media, the fast-food giant has officially confirmed which toys and cards you can collect from this round of the collaboration.

The Pokémon promotion launches November 10 in the U.S. and will expand to over 70 countries in the following months. The Happy Meal comes in three different boxes, each of which includes one of 15 Pokémon toys and two of 15 reprinted cards.

The specific list of cards Pokémon has revealed doesn’t exactly line up with what McDonald’s and leakers have been sharing online, and may in fact be leaks for next year's card list instead. The fast-food chain also hasn’t confirmed whether there will be any specific food or meal items — for now, it’s all about the collectibles.

The three Happy Meal boxes feature Pikachu, Torchic, and Umbreon. The toys are essentially mini versions of those boxes, displaying individual Pokémon's faces under the classic golden arches handle. While they may not be that fun to play with or big enough to use as an actual container, they at least require a little bit of effort to put together.

Here's the 15 pocket monsters that are getting the toy box treatment:

Like previous McDonald’s collaborations, the included cards are stamped reprints with McDonald’s numbering (M27, thus the potential confusion), and seven are confetti holo.

A full announcement on the Pokémon site includes a list of 15 cards, shown above, though Pokémon’s list differs from cards that McDonald’s accounts (and leakers) have been sharing on social media.

One McDonald’s announcement image has cards dedicated to Pikachu, Palafin, Mimikyu, Chandelure, Decidueye, Tyranitar. That list actually lines up with the cards leakers have been sharing online, which also include Zoroark, Wooloo, Snorlax, Eevee, Jirachi, Metagross, Absol, Hawlucha, and Lucario.

3 boxes. 15 toys. 2 cards with every collectible. Pokémon Happy Meal coming 11.10.26. https://t.co/mBO9iWzUTb

— McDonald's (@McDonalds) October 29, 2026


McDonald's accounts also confirm the promotion will be coming to over 70 countries over the next couple of months, with progressive launches through February next year. Toys and cards will likely vary by region, which may another reason for the card list confusion. For example, Quebec locations will not have the Happy Meal toys, instead offering a Pokémon sticker and a mini booster pack with four cards.

As for how much time Trainers will have to collect 'em all, Pokémon and McDonald’s are only going with “as long as supplies last.” X users, however, had been sharing images from their local McDonald’s store in the lead-up to the collaboration’s official announcement. One unconfirmed image shows the promotion running in U.S. locations from November 10 through December 14.

items.title: PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset Is Up for Preorder for $99, and It’s Out the Same Day as GTA 6
items.description: PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset preorders are live now. It's out November 19, the same day as GTA 6.
items.author: Chris Reed
items.content:
Heads up, PS5 owners: the PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset is now available for preorder. It comes in white or Midnight Black color schemes and is up at most of the usual retailers for $99. It's out November 19, which also happens to be the same day Grand Theft Auto VI releases. Coincidence? I honestly don’t know, but if you’re planning late-night GTA 6 sessions and don’t want to keep the roomies awake, having a brand-new pair of wireless headphones for your PS5 certainly won’t hurt.

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset - White

  • Get it at Amazon
  • Get it at Best Buy
  • Get it at PS Direct

The white version has a white headband, while the Midnight Black version has a black one.

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset - Midnight Black

  • Get it at Amazon
  • Get it at Best Buy
  • Get it at PS Direct

PlayStation Pulse Wireless Headset is a wireless headset designed for PS5 (naturally), with both PlayStation Link connectivity as well as Bluetooth, so it’ll work with other devices as well. It also features simultaneous connectivity, which lets you swap between, for instance, your PS5 and your phone instantly.

Sony touts it as having Tempest 3D audio support, which offers immersive sound that seems to come from all around you. It has planar magnetic drivers, which are supposed to produce “lifelike sound.” The built-in microphones let you do things like use in-game chat or talk on your phone, and it has “AI-enhanced noise rejection,” for clearer communication no matter what noise is going on in the background.

You can turn the earcups to flatten the headset out, making it easier to pack in a bag to take on the go. Basically, it’s a new Sony headset that ought to work excellently and seamlessly on the PS5. And it comes out the same day as GTA 6, giving you a good opportunity to try it out.

This new headset effectively replaces the Pulse 3D Wireless headset that we gave a 9/10 in our review. Here's hoping this new model is even better. I certainly like the look of the new one over the old one.

It's also worth noting that Sony is going to release the higher-end PlayStation Pulse Edge Wireless Headset, which was announced at the same time as this one, at some point early next year. It will feature active noise cancellation, but will cost more. The exact price and release date have yet to be announced.

In related news, for those who prefer earbuds to headphones, you can save $50 on PlayStation Pulse Explore Wireless Earbuds right now at Amazon.

items.title: The Hellraiser Franchise Is Getting Three New Tabletop Adaptations for Halloween 2027
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
Pinhead and the rest of the Hellraiser crew are seeing quite the resurgence right now, and that looks to continue into next year. Announced today, Salt Entertainment has revealed that they have entered an agreement with Clive Barker and Park Ave Ent. LLC to release not one, not two, but three official Hellraiser tabletop games with the first of these planned for release Halloween 2027. Perfectly timed to coincide with the 40th anniversary of the original film.

Salt’s currently slated hellish titles begin with Hellraiser: Puzzle of Flesh from designer Travis Chance (Cthulul: Dark Providence, Heroes Wanted) a dice-based / push-your-luck title themed around the franchise's signature Lament Configuration box. Coming in a custom box modeled after the artifact (which doubles as the game’s dice tumbler) Salt describes it as an “escape-room style and social deduction game in which hidden desires, shifting loyalties and questionable choices make it increasingly difficult to know whom - or what - to trust”. These devilish little boxes are some of the most recognizable relics from the films and I will be excited to see how what they represent gets adapted for the ol’ weekly game night when it releases next Halloween.

If you would prefer something more story driven, then you are in luck too as a fullblown Hellraiser tabletop RPG is also in the works. This project is being helmed by designer Franceso Nepitello who has a little experience in adapting big properties into TTRPGs, being the co-designer of The One Ring RPG based on the Lord of the Rings. Others may know him for another little game set in that universe, War of the Ring - a game we consider one of the best LoTR board games period. This RPG looks to allow fans to expand and open up the Hellraiser universe to let you explore and play out your own stories of temptation, desire, and the horrors that lie beyond our own world.

“I wanted to design a horror roleplaying game for years,” said Nepitello. “Getting to do it with Hellraiser is incredibly exciting. Its blend of dread, desire and forbidden knowledge offers so much to explore at the gaming table. I can’t wait to open the box with the players.”

Last up for this initial slate of games is the one I am most excited to learn more about. Headed up by game designer Michael Shinall, the guy behind other games such as Marvel Zombies, a Song of Ice & Fire: Tabletop Miniatures Game, Bloodborne: The Board Game, and most recently the Tasting History board game also being produced by Salt Entertainment (and currently on Kickstarter). Out of the three this is the one we know the least about, only being described as “a major new Hellraiser board game”, On the topic of working with such a legendary property, Shinall has a solid grasp on what this IP means, "Hellraiser is unique among the horror world as, outside brilliant monster and world design, it delves into the reaches of the human psyche in ways that many others have tried to emulate, but often failed to reach. It accepts that the truest horrors are never external, but the inner depths of the darkest parts of the soul... And I look forward to bringing that to a new medium."

Speaking with Geoff Skinner, President of Salt Entertainment regarding Barker’s input on these projects, he had this to say; “Yes, Clive Barker is approving everything and guiding our creative, so we are all on our A-game. We’re using not only the films as a basis, but also the original novella, Hellbound Heart. It’s always a treat to work with the original creator of any brand, but to be working with someone who shaped the culture so heavily is an absolute honor. He’s on such a hot streak with the Hellraiser video game (writer's note: check out our review we did here) and two hugely successful Kickstarter campaigns (comics and books), and we are thrilled to be a part of the Barkerverse. “

More details involving Puzzle of Flesh, the TTRPG, and Shinalls major board game project will be revealed over the coming months with the titles planned for release for the retail market.

items.title: Minecraft Creator Notch Is Selling His L.A. Mansion for the 'Low' Asking Price of $70 Million
items.description: Markus “Notch” Persson sold Minecraft developer Mojang to Microsoft back in 2014 for a cool $2.5 billion, then moved to the U.S. and casually outbid Jay-Z and Beyonce for a Beverly Hills mansion. At the time, it cost him $70 million. Now, he's selling up.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Markus “Notch” Persson sold Minecraft developer Mojang to Microsoft back in 2014 for a cool $2.5 billion, then moved to the U.S. and casually outbid Jay-Z and Beyonce for a Beverly Hills mansion. At the time, it cost him $70 million. Now, he's selling up.

Despite L.A.’s median home value more than doubling, Notch is looking for a quick sale on the mansion, a 22,300-square-foot estate which features 15 bathrooms, a $200,000 candy room, and its own private nightclub.

According to the L.A. Times, the market for housing for the super rich has cooled in the past decade, hence the “low” asking price.

If it sells, it’ll be the most expensive home sale in Beverly Hills this year and the second-priciest in L.A. County. When Notch bought it, the house boasted a 2,500-bottle wine cellar, and an art installation with a chrome machine gun as the centrepiece, as well as eight bedrooms, 15 bathrooms, a movie theatre and a swimming pool.

Notch added the nightclub, as well as a recording studio and a DJ booth to host parties for the rich and famous of Beverly Hills. According to Notch, he doesn’t spend much time in L.A. anymore, hence the sale.

Interestingly, he’s not alone. The listing coincided with a broader L.A. exit by tech moguls. Mark Zuckerberg and Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin have set up homes in Florida to avoid Proposition 40, a proposed wealth tax being voted on next week which would, if passed, levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California's billionaires.

Apparently, it’s a cause that’s united the rich. According to Politico, a record $612 million from more than 70 current and former California billionaires was pumped into this year’s state elections, with almost 50% of the funds aimed at defeating Proposition 40. Notch didn’t mention the tax as a reason for listing the property.

The Minecraft creator hasn’t put out any major video games since he sold Minecraft to Microsoft. The game is still one of the most popular in the world and continues to get regular updates. Microsoft recently launched Minecraft Dungeons 2, a sequel spinoff that turns the blocky Minecraft characters into warriors and mages in a Diablo-esque dungeon crawler. A Minecraft Movie, the big screen adaptation of the game, blew past $700 million at the box office. A sequel is in the works.

items.title: Dune: Part 3 Has 3 Popcorn Buckets, Including One With 2 Sandworm Mouths
items.description: With Dune: Part 3 fast approaching, AMC Theatres has finally shown off the movie's popcorn buckets. Fittingly, there are three.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
With Dune: Part 3 fast approaching, AMC Theatres has finally shown off the movie's popcorn buckets. Fittingly, there are three.

There’s one with two sandworm mouths, so you can share popcorn with other Dune-heads. Another features one mouth hole and a thumper that actually moves up and down while you munch your snacks.

The final popcorn-themed concession collectible is a bucket shaped like the mobile containment tank of the Guild Navigator, Edric, who we’ll likely get to know better in Dune: Part 3. The collectibles were officially revealed on the AMC Theatres Instagram page.

Dune: Part 3 is based on Frank Herbert's Dune Messiah, and takes place 17 years after the events of the first two films. Timothée Chalamet returns as Paul Atreides, who you know has probably gone too far this time because he’s shaved his head. Bald dudes mean business.

Meanwhile, Zendaya has an expanded role as Chaya and will reportedly campaign in the Best Actress category at the Oscars. Both previous Dune movies were nominated in technical excellence categories, but the actors didn’t get any nods.

Even if you think you know the book it’s based on, however, we might be in for some big surprises. The final trailer for Dune: Part 3 suggested some major deviations from the source material.

Dune: Part 2 surpassed the previous movie in the trilogy at the box office, generating almost $500 million. Dune: Part 1 grossed $433 million worldwide during its entire theatrical run. However, the first movie was released simultaneously in theaters and on HBO Max, giving people the option of watching it at home with their own popcorn buckets.

Dune: Part 3 is scheduled to release in cinemas on December 18, 2026, with early IMAX preview screenings beginning on December 14, 2026.

items.title: Some People Who Paid for WoW Forever Name Reservation Couldn't Reserve Their Name Due to a Weird Bug
items.description: After the World of Warcraft Forever beta ended last week, Blizzard opened up the servers to character creation in order to allow players who bought one of the Skyborne packs to reserve their names. But a lot of people were falsely given a "restricted" message when they tried to reserve their name.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
After the World of Warcraft Forever beta ended last week, Blizzard opened up the servers to character creation in order to allow players who bought one of the Skyborne packs to reserve their names. But a lot of people were falsely given a "restricted" message when they tried to reserve their name.

Even after the rough start that Blizzard's name reservation system had on Tuesday, some players weren't able to reserve their name, with the character creation screen telling them their name was on the restricted list. Blizzard has since fixed the problem, and told players it was due to a bugged name filter.

Community manager Kaivax took to the WoW Forever forums to explain: "In WoW Forever, we’ve been working on the restricted name list, which is a list the game uses to check for non-profane names that we wish to restrict, such as major Warcraft lore characters or names that are blocked for technical reasons. Today we’ve determined that we have a bug in the process that caused the game to be overly restrictive with some names. For example, it has been incorrectly restricting names containing 'c-o-n.'"

In the replies to Kaivax's post, it was made clear that the name filter was a bit overzealous. Player Nursejoy posted: "Major Warcraft lore characters? I understand that but it seems any named NPC is on the list. Example: Generically named NPCs 'Nurse' and 'Officer' hardly hold major Warcraft lore but names containing 'nurse' are restricted. This is a specifically bad example to illustrate impact." They then went on to list 23 different character names with the word 'nurse' that they supposedly tried to reserve, but couldn't.

According to Kaivax, the fixes should have gone live with the server restart, but some players are still reporting problems reserving their names. However, I've been able to go in and reserve the name 'Concon Concon,' so the specific combination that Kaivax mentioned does seem to have been fixed at least.

But while this overly strict name filter appears to have been a bug, WoW Forever has been fairly strict on character names. There was a controversy relatively early in the beta about names being reported, and Blizzard had to come out and reassure players that humans were reviewing the reports. I also got a chance to sit down with WoW Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut to talk about the future of the game, and it seems like the team is laser-focused on making it an even more social version of the MMO.

items.title: FromSoftware's Nintendo Switch 2 Exclusive The Duskbloods Officially Delayed Into 2027
items.description: FromSoftware has announced a delay of The Duskbloods to 2027. The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive was due out by the end of 2026.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
FromSoftware has announced a delay of The Duskbloods to 2027. The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive was due out by the end of 2026.

In a statement published online, the Dark Souls and Elden Ring developer said that it had decided to delay the game following feedback from the recent network test, with a focus on combat, strategic depth, and player expression.

There’s no word on when in 2027 The Duskbloods will launch.

Fans had braced themselves for a delay after The Duskblood was among a number of no-shows at the September 2026 Nintendo Direct. Before that, in August, FromSoftware brought The Duskbloods network test to an early end after the first day of testing resulted in "game server issues" that barred players from logging in.

FromSoftware is responsible for some of the most influential games of the last 20 years, including 2022 masterpiece Elden Ring. So anticipation for The Duskbloods to recreate some of that FromSoftware magic on Switch 2 is sky high.

Until there is more to share, you can read IGN's interview with FromSoftware's Hidetaka Miyazaki. You can also check out our preview.

Here's FromSoftware's statement in full:

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support.

During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

items.title: Bloodborne Movie Gets Promising Update from Producer Jacksepticeye
items.description: Seán "Jacksepticeye" McLoughlin has provided an exclusive and promising update on the Bloodborne film to IGN.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Seán "Jacksepticeye" McLoughlin has provided an exclusive and promising update on the Bloodborne film to IGN.

While speaking with IGN about becoming the new elusive target in Hitman (out today), we naturally had to ask McLoughlin for an update on the Bloodborne movie, which he is producing. I pointed out that it's been over six months since the animated film was first announced, and at that time, it didn't have a writer or a director attached. McLoughlin confirmed to IGN that the film now has a writer and a director, and the movie is making great progress.

"Things are obviously much more along the pipeline than they were back then," he said. "It's one of those things that I personally would love to just say everything as a fan of this thing, but then there's no expectation, or there's no fun in the process. So we definitely have a lot more stuff mapped out where we're going with the story, and there are people in place to make this thing happen. Hopefully sooner than later, we can have announcements where we talk about who's involved and where it's going, and little teases of the story and where we're at with that.

"But I am proud of the work I've been doing on it. I think it's such an interesting job to have, and for me, it's fun to do. It can be really stressful as well at the same time because you're taking on such a monumental IP. And I am just there to be like, 'Hey, we need this pinprick perfect.' Will we ever get something perfect? I don't know. It's probably impossible to get everyone's expectations into one central pillar, but as someone who's brought on to do this job, I'm right in the position where I need to be, and we're poised to have something really cool."

As of right now, the team behind the film is keeping a lid on who the writer and director are. It's unclear when we'll learn more, but there are ample opportunities for reveals on the horizon - perhaps at The Game Awards this December, or during another gaming event next year. Speaking more about how the team is trying to translate Bloodborne to a new medium, McLoughlin noted that there's a big difference in how Bloodborne is an animated movie and Alex Garland's Elden Ring will be live action.

"We all have pie-in-the-sky dreams of doing that and making a huge story. And I guess we'll see what happens with Elden Ring, but even I don't think they're doing [the entirety of] Elden Ring. I'm sure they pick one part of that to be able to do because I mean, it'll cost you $600 million to do Elden Ring in live action.

"It's just the amount of time, effort, pieces moving, the amount of financials needed in place; is it even a smart decision to do it live action at that point, when there's a lot of stuff that you'd be able to do in animation that you can't do in live action, or you wouldn't nail down? And I think Bloodborne specifically is poised to do that well, because there's so much otherworldly aspects in that that would just be so cool to be able to blow the doors off animated rather than being like, 'Okay, put you in front of a green screen, and let's hope for the best.' Now, we can really whittle it down into something cool."

On the subject of the Elden Ring film, I also asked if his team has a plan to take any lessons from that project and apply it to the Bloodborne movie, or if there's such a difference in how they're making their respective movies that it won't be applicable.

"I mean, probably a bit of both. It is sort of a thing that it'll come out before ours. So you look at it and go, 'Okay, well, what did they do? What was their idea? Are we doing the similar things?' But I mean, Bloodborne and Elden Ring are so far apart from each other. The structure maybe is similar, but in terms of story [one is] Victorian England [and the other is] gods and a mountain [which are] very different from each other. So I would like to not take influence too much because you don't want to repeat the same things. And if it comes out, people are going to be upset, happy, indifferent. It's going to be a huge wide gamut of what people enjoy about different things. So hopefully give something people they don't expect, give them something that's interesting. And at the end of the day, it's all 'Why are we adapting it?'

"I don't want to adapt something if we're just going to tell the same stories with the same characters over and over and over again. Movies are a completely different medium than video games. What do movies do better than a game does? It's passive versus interactive, so how do we push and pull with that and play with different ideas? I think I don't want to be involved in an adaptation if it doesn't feel like there's a story worth telling within it or if it's not a good idea."

He went on to note that this isn't the first time he's taken a crack at a video game adaptation, as he'd previously tried to bring Soma to life, as well.
